Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            selfLink:
              title: Self link
              description: >-
                A relative link to this owner's resource, formed as
                '/api/owners/' followed by the owner's id.
              type: string
              example: '/api/owners/1'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: >-
                The pet owner's salutation, composed as the title and last name
                separated by a single space (e.g. 'DR who'), or just the last
                name when no title was supplied.
              type: string
              example: 'DR Franklin'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel: 'EMAIL' when an email
                address is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 'telephone' formatted for humans: a '+' and the
                country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in threes
                (e.g. '+61412345678' becomes '+61 412 345 678'). The raw
                'telephone' stays in canonical E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            memberId:
              title: Member ID
              description: >-
                A stable member id assigned on create, formatted
                '<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>': REGION is the region code derived
                from the owner's postcode (falling back to the city), FY is the
                two-digit fiscal year of the business-day-adjusted
                registrationDate (the fiscal year starts on 1 July), HASH8 is
                the first eight upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 digest
                of the normalized telephone concatenated with the last name, and
                CHK is a single Luhn check digit computed over the digits of
                '<REGION><FY><HASH8>'. When the computed id collides with an
                already-registered owner's it is de-duplicated by appending
                '-<n>' with the smallest n of 2 or more that makes it unique.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW261A2B3C4D5'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for owners that belong to the same
                household. Owners created with 'sharesHousehold' set true that
                match an existing owner's lastName and address are assigned the
                same householdId as that household.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-3F2A1B9C7D4E'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived identity key, formed as the normalized
                telephone, the email (or an empty string when absent) and the
                householdId joined by '|'. This single key is the sole basis for
                duplicate detection on create: a new owner is rejected with 409
                only when its whole identityKey equals an existing owner's.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|HH-3F2A1B9C7D4E'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners at the time of creation that share
                this owner's firstName and lastName, compared case-insensitively
                (not counting this owner). Assigned on create.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-
                The fiscal year of the business-day-adjusted registrationDate,
                formatted 'FY<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the fiscal
                year. The fiscal year starts on 1 July and is identified by the
                calendar year in which it ends. Absent when no registrationDate
                has been assigned.
              type: string
              example: 'FY26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points, assigned on create: starting at
                0, plus 2 when an email address is present, plus 1 when
                namesakeCount is 0, plus 2 for a household of 3 or more members,
                plus 3 when the owner's tenure is more than one fiscal year.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level from 1 to 4, derived from
                membershipPoints: level 1 for 0-1 points, level 2 for 2-3
                points, level 3 for 4-5 points and level 4 for 6 or more points.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The canonical region derived from the owner's city using a fixed
                city-to-region table (Sydney -> NSW, Melbourne -> VIC,
                Brisbane -> QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The owner's IANA timezone name derived from the locality/region
                using a fixed region-to-timezone table (NSW -> Australia/Sydney,
                VIC -> Australia/Melbourne, QLD -> Australia/Brisbane). Absent
                when the region is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            ownerSegment:
              title: Owner segment
              description: >-
                The owner's segment, formatted '<TIER>_<AREA>'. TIER is
                'PREMIUM' when membershipLevel is 3 or more, otherwise
                'STANDARD'. AREA is 'METRO' when the locality is a known
                region (NSW, VIC or QLD), otherwise 'REGIONAL'.
              type: string
              enum:
                - PREMIUM_METRO
                - PREMIUM_REGIONAL
                - STANDARD_METRO
                - STANDARD_REGIONAL
              example: 'STANDARD_METRO'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-
                The owner's age band derived from 'birthDate' relative to the
                'registrationDate': 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from 18 to 64
                inclusive, and 'SENIOR' at 65 or older. Absent when no birthDate
                was supplied.
              type: string
              enum:
                - MINOR
                - ADULT
                - SENIOR
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners had already been created for this
                owner's registration date at the time this owner was created,
                otherwise false. Assigned on create.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            capacityWarning:
              title: Capacity warning
              description: >-
                True when this owner's city already held between 40 and 49
                owners (inclusive) at the time this owner was created, meaning
                it is approaching the per-city capacity limit of 50; otherwise
                false. Assigned on create.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when this owner, though not a hard duplicate, was created
                sharing an existing owner's lastName and postcode with a
                different telephone, otherwise false. Assigned on create.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of
              description: >-
                The id of the existing owner this owner soft-matches on lastName
                and postcode when 'possibleDuplicate' is true; absent otherwise.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            riskFlag:
              title: Risk flag
              description: >-
                True when any of these hold: this owner is a possible duplicate
                ('possibleDuplicate' is true), the owner's email domain is
                disposable-adjacent (it shares its registrable domain label with
                a known disposable domain — a different top-level domain or a
                subdomain of one), or the owner's city currently holds more than
                its soft capacity of 40 owners; otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            deleted:
              title: Deleted
              description: >-
                Whether this owner has been soft-deleted. A newly created owner
                is false; DELETE /api/owners/{id} flags it true while retaining
                the record. Deleted owners are ignored by the create endpoint's
                duplicate and identity checks.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array

The refactoring is complete. Here's a summary of what I did and why.

## What I found

The upcoming V2 change forks a single concept — "the region code" — into two that must diverge: the region *stamped inside identifiers* (which gains a `V2` tag so every identifier changes) versus the *plain user-facing region* (`locality`, which must stay `NSW`). The existing code made that fork dangerous in one specific way:

- `OwnerMapper.locality` and `OwnerMapper.fiscalYear` didn't derive their values from source data. They **parsed the values back out of the `memberId` string** (via the `identityRegion` / `memberIdCore` helpers that split the identifier into `REGION` + `FY(2)` + `HASH8(8)` + `CHK(1)`). So the user-facing `locality` was literally whatever region was embedded in the member id. Under V2, that embedded region gets the `V2` tag — which would have silently corrupted `locality`, `timezone`, and the segment area, all of which must stay plain.

## What I changed (behavior-preserving)

1. **Decoupled the user-facing fields from the identifier internals** (`OwnerMapper`):
   - `locality(owner)` now derives the plain region straight from `cityRegionResolver.regionFor(city, postcode)` instead of reading it out of the `memberId`.
   - `fiscalYear(owner)` now derives from `registrationDate` directly instead of parsing the `memberId`'s FY segment.
   - Removed the now-unused `identityRegion` and `memberIdCore` back-parsing helpers.
   - These values are provably equal today (the member id's region *is* `regionFor(city, postcode)`, its FY *is* `fiscalYear(registrationDate)`), so nothing changes now — but they're no longer hostage to the identifier's internal format.

2. **Named the identifier-region seam** (`CityRegionResolver.identityRegionFor`): a single authority-owned method for "the region stamped inside identifiers," documented as deliberately distinct from the locality region. `OwnerRegistrar.memberId` now routes through it. Today it delegates to `regionFor`; V2 changes only this one method body to mix in the `V2` tag, and the other two identifiers can reuse the same seam.

I deliberately left `OwnerAuditor` and the identity derivations of `identityKey`/`householdId` untouched — they follow the codebase's established pattern (derived values computed in the mapper and passed in), so V2 lands there as localized additions rather than needing structural prep now.

## Verification

The only test, `AcceptanceTest`, is the held-out oracle for the *V2* change (it asserts `apiVersion: 2` and a nested `identity` object) and correctly still fails on those assertions — implementing V2 is explicitly out of scope. Crucially, its dumped response body is **byte-for-byte identical** before and after my refactor (`locality: NSW`, `memberId: NSW2716E6609E1`, `fiscalYear: FY27`, `ownerSegment: STANDARD_METRO`, `timezone: Australia/Sydney`, unchanged `householdId`/`identityKey`), confirming behavior is preserved exactly and the code compiles and runs.

   - Removed the now-unused `identityRegion` and `memberIdCore` back-parsing helpers.
   - These values are provably equal today (the member id's region *is* `regionFor(city, postcode)`, its FY *is* `fiscalYear(registrationDate)`), so nothing changes now — but they're no longer hostage to the identifier's internal format.

2. **Named the identifier-region seam** (`CityRegionResolver.identityRegionFor`): a single authority-owned method for "the region stamped inside identifiers," documented as deliberately distinct from the locality region. `OwnerRegistrar.memberId` now routes through it. Today it delegates to `regionFor`; V2 changes only this one method body to mix in the `V2` tag, and the other two identifiers can reuse the same seam.

I deliberately left `OwnerAuditor` and the identity derivations of `identityKey`/`householdId` untouched — they follow the codebase's established pattern (derived values computed in the mapper and passed in), so V2 lands there as localized additions rather than needing structural prep now.
